args: Analyze the root cause and best minimal fix for unchecked span arithmetic in `InverseBlitter::blitH` and `InverseBlitter::prepost` in `skia/src/core/SkScan_Path.cpp`. Specifically determine the invariants of fFirstX/fLastX/fPrevX, whether incoming ordinary spans should be intersected with the inverse clip, and whether clamping endpoints before subtraction preserves inverse-fill semantics. Also note any analogous implementation elsewhere in Skia.

The supplied ASan report crashes from InverseBlitter::prepost into SkRectClipBlitter and SkARGB32_Blitter. The reported sequence is that `fPrevX = x + width` overflows or yields an endpoint outside the inverse clip, then `fLastX - fPrevX` wraps positive and emits a malformed span. This occurs for a non-AA inverse-filled extreme transformed path. I am considering fixing InverseBlitter itself by clamping each incoming span interval/end to [fFirstX,fLastX] with overflow-safe comparisons/subtraction, and ensuring prepost only emits when fPrevX < fLastX. Need preserve semantics for spans wholly outside either side and unusual ordering.
